 Jisoo Brings Her Childhood Creation Shumon To Life In “Sun Showers” Video
 Nov 20, 2026 
 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Linkedin ReddIt Email Print 
 Prefer us on Google 
 Jisoo has found a pretty spectacular way to introduce the world to a character she invented in middle school. The BLACKPINK superstar’s original song “Sun Showers,” recorded for ‘The Angry Birds Movie 3’, comes with an animated music video starring Shumon, a fluffy, dustball-inspired creature she dreamed up and drew years before becoming a global pop sensation.
 The character appears on the single’s cover art and serves as Jisoo’s animated alter ego throughout the video. Shumon performs for a roaring stadium crowd, dances alongside the Angry Birds characters at a disco and shares the screen with familiar feathered faces and mischievous pigs. There are also glimpses of the film itself and hidden surprises for eagle-eyed viewers.
 It’s a wonderfully personal touch for a major animated movie soundtrack. Something Jisoo created as a schoolgirl has become part of a global entertainment franchise.
 Musically, “Sun Showers” is pure feel-good synth-pop, packed with bright melodies, buoyant production and Jisoo’s unmistakably sweet vocals. The song takes its title seriously, pairing the idea of unexpected sunshine with a message about finding happiness when circumstances aren’t ideal. Its cheerful sound is particularly effective because the production gives Jisoo plenty of room to deliver a melody that sticks around after the song ends.
 “Happiness will multiply when the sun is on your side,” she sings, summing up the song’s optimistic spirit.
 Jisoo co-wrote the track specifically for ‘The Angry Birds Movie 3’, which opens in theatres on December 23, 2026. Audiences first heard a preview in the film’s second trailer, introducing her contribution to a franchise known for its colourful characters and chaotic humour.
 “I’m so happy to be part of The Angry Birds Movie 3. I’ve always loved how the films bring together such colorful characters, humor, and heart,” Jisoo told The Hollywood Reporter.
 The animated video makes especially good use of her playful side. Shumon’s journey from an imaginary childhood drawing to a singing, dancing character feels like a charming extension of Jisoo’s creative personality, and the connection gives the song a story beyond its soundtrack origins.
 “Sun Showers” also arrives during a busy stretch of solo music for the singer, who is developing her first full-length solo album.
 Her previously released single “Addicted” explores the exhilarating rush of overwhelming attraction through glossy dance-pop production. “Click” approaches romance from another direction, capturing the unexpected connection between two people who seem to inhabit entirely different worlds.
 The Joseph Kahn-directed video for “Click” offers another glimpse of Jisoo’s imaginative visual storytelling. She portrays the last sentient cyborg in an abandoned theme park, accompanied by Click Bear, a character symbolizing her worldwide fan community. Together, they transform the deserted surroundings into a lively environment filled with music and movement.
 Between Click Bear and Shumon, Jisoo is developing a colourful collection of characters that give her solo releases an extra layer of personality. Her willingness to revisit an idea from childhood also adds something genuinely endearing to the ‘Angry Birds’ collaboration.
 The result is a soundtrack contribution with a wonderfully unlikely origin story. “Sun Showers” delivers the cheerful pop hook a family animated film deserves, while Shumon gets the kind of big-screen adventure that a middle-school imagination could only dream about.
